definitions.definition: Serious mental or physical suffering.
definitions.example_sentence: Nkem watched with anguish as her trophies were destroyed.
practice_sentences: She stared at the wreckage in [anguish].
His face showed the [anguish] he felt after the loss.
They cried out in [anguish] when they heard the news.

definitions.definition: To experience great distress or suffering.
definitions.example_sentence: Jayden told himself he wouldn't anguish over his homework.
practice_sentences: He continued to [anguish] over the difficult decision.
She [anguished] for days after the argument.
Don't [anguish] over things you cannot change.

definitions.definition: To make changes to gradually improve something.
definitions.example_sentence: Bridget liked to hone her fishing skills whenever she could.
practice_sentences: She spent years trying to [hone] her writing skills.
He [honed] his craft through constant practice.
Athletes must [hone] their techniques before competition.

definitions.definition: To make a blade sharper.
definitions.example_sentence: The blacksmith had to hone the blade until it was sharp.
practice_sentences: He carefully [honed] the knife before cutting the meat.
The chef [hones] her knives every morning.
Workers used a stone to [hone] the old axe.

definitions.definition: To reduce or limit something.
definitions.example_sentence: The manager needed to curtail how much the company spent.
practice_sentences: The government decided to [curtail] public spending.
She had to [curtail] her trip due to bad weather.
New rules will [curtail] the use of plastic bags.

definitions.definition: To agree to something.
definitions.example_sentence: Babs was happy to assent to Lou's offer of a motorcycle ride.
practice_sentences: He reluctantly [assented] to the new plan.
The board will [assent] to the proposal tomorrow.
She [assents] to almost every request from her boss.

definitions.definition: The act of showing that you agree with or approve of something.
definitions.example_sentence: Magnus signalled his assent to the terms of the contract.
practice_sentences: The committee gave its [assent] to the merger.
He nodded in [assent] without saying a word.
Her [assent] was needed before the deal could close.

definitions.definition: To win.
definitions.example_sentence: The contestant who has prepared the most will prevail.
practice_sentences: In the end, justice will [prevail].
The underdog team [prevailed] against all odds.
Good always seems to [prevail] in fairy tales.

definitions.definition: To be widespread at a certain time or in a certain place.
definitions.example_sentence: When they see our powerful army, fear will prevail throughout the land.
practice_sentences: Calm conditions [prevailed] across the region this week.
A sense of hope [prevails] among the survivors.
Poverty still [prevails] in many parts of the world.

definitions.definition: To think carefully about something.
definitions.example_sentence: Cole got very lost and had to ponder which direction to fly in.
practice_sentences: She sat quietly, trying to [ponder] her next move.
He [pondered] the question for several minutes.
They [ponder] over the mysterious letter for hours.

definitions.definition: Trying to impress by making yourself seem more important or talented than you are.
definitions.example_sentence: The pretentious new chef bragged about serving an eight-course meal.
practice_sentences: His [pretentious] speech annoyed most of the guests.
She found his art collection a bit [pretentious].
They mocked the [pretentious] way he described his job.

definitions.definition: Causing great sadness.
definitions.example_sentence: The main characters reunite in this poignant final scene.
practice_sentences: It was a deeply [poignant] farewell between the friends.
The film's ending felt especially [poignant].
Her [poignant] letter brought tears to his eyes.

definitions.definition: The state of being boring or bored.
definitions.example_sentence: Eli found many ways to overcome the tedium of studying.
practice_sentences: She tried to escape the [tedium] of her daily commute.
The long meeting was full of [tedium].
He broke up the [tedium] with a few jokes.

definitions.definition: To stop someone succeeding at something.
definitions.example_sentence: We managed to thwart his attempt to take over the world.
practice_sentences: The heavy rain [thwarted] their plans for a picnic.
Security guards [thwarted] the robbery.
Her efforts to [thwart] the merger ultimately failed.

definitions.definition: The feel of a material or substance.
definitions.example_sentence: Neil's cake had the perfect fluffy texture.
practice_sentences: The fabric had a rough [texture] against her skin.
He admired the smooth [texture] of the marble.
The soup had a creamy [texture].

definitions.definition: To add a raised or rough feel to something.
definitions.example_sentence: Marina wanted to texture the sculpture to make it more realistic.
practice_sentences: The artist decided to [texture] the wall before painting it.
She [textured] the icing to look like tree bark.
They [texture] the ceiling to hide imperfections.

definitions.definition: Either the soft light when the sun has just set or is about to rise, or the time during which this light occurs.
definitions.example_sentence: Vincent admired the sky's changing colours at twilight.
practice_sentences: Birds sang softly as [twilight] settled over the hills.
They walked home together at [twilight].
The sky glowed orange during [twilight].

definitions.definition: The final part or gradual decline of something.
definitions.example_sentence: Penelope is now in the twilight of her career.
practice_sentences: The old champion fought on in the [twilight] of his career.
The empire entered the [twilight] of its power.
She wrote her memoirs in the [twilight] of her life.

definitions.definition: Looking old, thin or damaged due to being used a lot.
definitions.example_sentence: There was only a threadbare sofa in the tiny living room.
practice_sentences: He wore a [threadbare] coat to keep out the cold.
The [threadbare] carpet needed replacing.
Her old jeans were completely [threadbare].

definitions.definition: Either a gas or small drops of liquid that form a fine mist in the air.
definitions.example_sentence: A foul-smelling vapour was coming from Maria's dinner.
practice_sentences: [Vapour] rose from the boiling kettle.
The chemist studied the strange [vapour] in the lab.
Clouds of [vapour] drifted across the cold morning air.

definitions.definition: A state of disruption or confusion.
definitions.example_sentence: After the earthquake, the village was in turmoil.
practice_sentences: The country descended into political [turmoil].
Her mind was in [turmoil] after the shocking news.
The market experienced great [turmoil] last year.

definitions.definition: Rude or lacking decency.
definitions.example_sentence: Viraj couldn't stand his cousin's uncouth behaviour.
practice_sentences: His [uncouth] manners embarrassed the whole family.
She was shocked by his [uncouth] remarks at dinner.
They found his [uncouth] jokes offensive.
